wine.name: Txomin Etxaniz
wine.grapes: Mostly Hondarrabi Zuri, with a share of Hondarrabi Beltza that merchants' sheets put at anything from a twentieth to a half; the house's own sheet names Hondarrabi Zuri alone.
wine.sites: The family's own vineyards in Getaria, on slopes that fall to the Cantabrian Sea, within the original zone of the Getariako Txakolina DO.
wine.making: Picked by hand at the start of October, by the house's sheet, and pressed in a pneumatic press under inert gas. The must is fermented at a controlled temperature in stainless steel tanks, and the wine rests on its lees until bottling, holding some of the fermentation's own carbon dioxide, which gives its faint natural prickle.
wine.glass: Pale greenish yellow with a fine natural bead; lemon and fresh green apple over a stony, salty edge. Very dry and light, with the sharp acidity of Getaria and a gentle prickle on a clean finish.
wine.ageing: Made to be drunk young, within a year or so of the harvest, while its prickle and its sharp fruit are fresh; it is not a wine to lay down.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, the house itself advising a little colder; no decanter; poured from a height into a wide tumbler in the Basque way, or into a white wine glass.

label.means: The DO of Getaria, the first of the three txakoli DOs, recognised in 1989 and widened to all Gipuzkoa in 2007.
Txakoli in Basque with its article; chacolí in Spanish.
The family house of Getaria, named after a forebear in the family's line.

records.table: Txomin Etxaniz is a Getaria family's white txakoli, from vines its records place there from 1649: mostly Hondarrabi Zuri from slopes above the sea, pale, sharp and faintly prickling. Pour it from a height into a tumbler, beside anchovies or grilled fish.
records.story: The family behind Txomin Etxaniz traces its vines in Getaria to 1649, when the notarial archives of Gipuzkoa record a forebear tending vines in the town. The house sets out its line through later generations it marks at 1859, 1899 and 1922, and it carries the name of Txomin Etxaniz, one of those forebears. In 1980, by its own account and in others, a new generation of the family, of the Txueka Etxaniz line, set out to revive Getaria's txakoli: to keep to the old Hondarrabi grapes, to modernise the cellar and to win a protected name for the wine of the coast. That name came by an order of 21 September 1989, which recognised Getariako Txakolina for Getaria, Zarautz and Aia, the first of the three txakoli DOs; the family is counted among those who pressed for it. In 2007 the zone was widened to the whole of Gipuzkoa. The house grows its grapes on its own slopes above the sea, ferments in temperature controlled steel and makes a rosé, a sparkling wine and a late harvest wine beside its white. For a sommelier its white is the plain statement of Getariako Txakolina: low in alcohol, sharp, faintly prickling and made to be drunk within the year.

others.name: Txomin Etxaniz Rosado
others.note: The house's rosé txakoli, from its own vineyards in Getaria.

others.name: Eugenia
others.note: The house's sparkling white txakoli, made by the traditional method from Hondarrabi Zuri, by its sheet.

others.name: Uydi
others.note: A late harvest txakoli of Hondarrabi Zuri from old vines, picked in November, by the house's sheet.

traps: Txomin Etxaniz is the house and its white both: the name is a forebear of the family, not a grape or a village.
Getariako Txakolina was the first txakoli DO, in 1989; Bizkaiko Txakolina followed in 1994 and Arabako Txakolina in 2001.
Its prickle is the fermentation's own carbon dioxide held in the wine: it is not a sparkling wine made by a second fermentation.

cards.front: Txomin Etxaniz: from what year do the family's records place its vines in Getaria?
cards.back: 1649, when the notarial archives of Gipuzkoa record a forebear of the family tending vines there.

cards.front: Which grape leads the blend of the Txomin Etxaniz white?
cards.back: Hondarrabi Zuri, the white grape of txakoli, with a share of Hondarrabi Beltza in most merchants' accounts.

questions.q: A guest asks why the Txomin Etxaniz white tingles faintly on the tongue. Which explanation is right?
opts: Its own carbon dioxide, kept from the fermentation
A second fermentation in the bottle
Carbon dioxide pumped in before bottling
A second fermentation in a sealed tank
questions.exp: The house ferments at a controlled temperature in steel and keeps the wine on its lees until bottling, and its sheet speaks of a fine natural bead; no second fermentation is made, so it is not a sparkling wine.

questions.q: The family of Txomin Etxaniz is counted among those who pressed for Getaria's protected name. When was Getariako Txakolina recognised as a DO?
questions.exp: An order of 21 September 1989 recognised Getariako Txakolina, the first txakoli DO; 1994 is the year of Bizkaia's DO, and 2007 the year Getaria's zone was widened to all Gipuzkoa.

report: Searches for this record: 5 of the group's share of 35; one fetch tried, of the house's technical sheet, refused (the host does not resolve here), and the house's site was read through search on txominetxaniz.com.

The plan's note is answered: the 1649 record is the house's own account and is repeated by Cellar Tours and Wine Spectator, which name the protocol archives of Gipuzkoa; the 1980 revival is on the house's family page and on two secondary pages; the family's part in the DO of 1989 rests on the house and on two secondary pages, so the story says it is counted among those who pressed for it.
Founded is empty: 1649 is the first record of the family's vines, not the founding of the winery, and no source gives a founding year for the bodega.

The white's grapes disagree: the house's sheets name Hondarrabi Zuri alone, Cellar Tours and an importer give nine tenths Hondarrabi Zuri with Hondarrabi Beltza, and Decanter's note of the 2020 gives 85 and 15 per cent; the record says the great majority with a small share of Beltza in most accounts.

The house advises 5 to 8 degrees Celsius; the record follows the 8 to 10 the Codex gives a light white, with the house's colder advice beside it. The harvest is the start of October on the house's sheet and the end of September on an importer's page; the record gives the house's.

Wine Spectator's article (its address carries a living writer's name, so it is not cited) says the wine is named for the uncle of a living family member's grandfather and that Txomin is the Basque Domingo; the record says only that the name is a forebear's, on the house's family page, which sets Txomin Etxaniz at 1899.

Living people met and not named: the family member said to have led the revival of 1980 and the present generation; the Txueka Etxaniz line is named as a family, as the house names it. Not in WINE_PRODUCERS.

wine.name: Rubentis
wine.grapes: Hondarrabi Beltza and Hondarrabi Zuri, about half of each by its importer's and a Spanish guide's accounts, picked and worked together.
wine.sites: The family's vineyards on the hills above Getaria and Zarautz, looking out to the sea, trained high on the parral, the old Basque pergola that lifts the bunches into the wind.
wine.making: The black and white grapes are picked by hand, destemmed together and pressed directly. The must is fermented with native yeasts in stainless steel at about 15 degrees Celsius for some twenty days, and the tank is closed towards the end so the wine keeps its own carbon dioxide; the house never carbonates by force.
wine.glass: Pale pink; wild strawberry, cherry and watermelon over a salty, briny snap. Bone dry and light in body, with cutting acidity and a gentle natural prickle.
wine.ageing: Made for the summer after the harvest and drunk within the year, while the fruit is bright and the prickle lively; it is not meant to age.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no decanter; poured from a height into a wide tumbler as in Getaria, or into a white wine glass, as an aperitif or beside grilled fish.

label.means: The name of Ameztoi's still rosé of Hondarrabi Beltza and Hondarrabi Zuri.
The family house of Getaria that makes it, at a winery looking out to the sea.
The DO of Getaria, recognised in 1989 for Getaria, Zarautz and Aia and widened to all Gipuzkoa in 2007.

records.table: Rubentis is Ameztoi's rosé from Getaria: Hondarrabi Beltza and Hondarrabi Zuri in about equal parts, fermented together with native yeasts and bottled with its own gentle prickle. Pale, salty and full of wild strawberry, it is poured from a height as an aperitif.
records.story: The Ameztoi family has made txakoli in Getaria since 1820 by its own account, and tells of five generations at the work; its American importer gives 1860, so the year of the start is left open. Its vineyards climb the hills behind Getaria and Zarautz, trained high on the parral, the old Basque pergola that lifts the grapes into the wind off the Bay of Biscay and dries them after rain. When the Getariako Txakolina DO was recognised by an order of 21 September 1989, the family's vines lay within its first zone of Getaria, Zarautz and Aia, and in 2007 the zone was widened to the whole of Gipuzkoa. The house says the colour of Rubentis recalls the old txakoli of the Cantabrian coast: white Hondarrabi Zuri and black Hondarrabi Beltza picked and fermented together, and bottled with the natural prickle that is the habit of Getaria rather than gas added at bottling. The rosé became the house's other face beside its classic white, a pink txakoli for the summer, and it had a son: Hijo de Rubentis, a sparkling rosé made by the traditional method and aged some three years in the cellar on average, by the house's account. For a sommelier Rubentis shows the black grape of the coast, and that txakoli can be pink and keep its salt and its prickle.

others.name: Ameztoi
others.note: The family's classic white txakoli of Getaria, the house's other wine to know.

others.name: Hijo de Rubentis
others.note: The son of Rubentis: a traditional method sparkling rosé of Hondarrabi Beltza and Hondarrabi Zuri, aged some three years in the cellar on average, by the house's account.

traps: Rubentis is a still rosé with a natural prickle; Hijo de Rubentis is the sparkling one, made by the traditional method.
Zuri is white and beltza black: Rubentis needs both grapes, in about equal parts, picked and fermented together.
Rubentis is Getariako Txakolina, from Gipuzkoa, not Bizkaiko Txakolina, the DO of the province of Bilbao.

cards.front: Rubentis: which two grapes go into it, and in what proportion?
cards.back: Hondarrabi Beltza and Hondarrabi Zuri, about half of each, picked and fermented together.

cards.front: How are Ameztoi's vines above Getaria trained, and why?
cards.back: High on the parral, the old Basque pergola, which lifts the bunches into the sea wind to dry them after rain.

questions.q: A guest wonders how Ameztoi's Rubentis keeps its gentle prickle. What does the house do?
opts: Closes the tank near the end of fermentation
Adds carbon dioxide just before bottling
Ferments the wine again in its bottle
Blends in a little sparkling wine
questions.exp: The tank is closed towards the end of fermentation so the wine keeps its own gas, and the house never carbonates by force; a second fermentation in bottle is the way of Hijo de Rubentis.

questions.q: By the Ameztoi family's own account, since what year has it made txakoli in Getaria?
questions.exp: The family's own pages give 1820 and five generations; 1649 is the year the Txomin Etxaniz family's records in Getaria begin, and 1989 the year of the DO.

report: Searches for this record: 5 of the group's share of 35, no fetch tried; the house's own site was read through search on txakoliameztoi.com, and the importer De Maison through search on its domain.

The plan's note is answered: Rubentis is labelled Getariako Txakolina; the blend is about half of each grape on De Maison's and Spanish Wine Lover's pages and a mixture of the two on the house's, and one merchant's ninety to ten is taken for a slip; the house gives 1820 and five generations, De Maison 1860, and other pages seven generations, so founded is empty and the story hedges.

Left out for want of a second source: De Maison's old vineyard of Hondarrabi Beltza planted in 1840, its six months on the lees with stirring (one merchant), the year Rubentis was first made (found nowhere), and the meaning of the name Rubentis (found nowhere).

The parral rests on the house's own page and on a machinery maker's case history of the estate; the tank closed at the end of fermentation on a merchant's page and De Maison's never forced carbonation; native yeasts and 15 degrees Celsius for about twenty days on De Maison and a merchant.
The glass draws on the house's strawberry and cherry and on two merchants' notes (wild strawberry, watermelon, salty, bone dry with a gentle fizz).
Living people met and not named: the fifth generation named in the sources. Not in WINE_PRODUCERS.

wine.name: Itsasmendi 7
wine.grapes: Hondarrabi Zuri and Hondarrabi Zuri Zerratia, the Basque name for Petit Courbu, the great majority, with a share of Riesling.
wine.sites: A selection from several of the house's own plots across Bizkaia, by its own account, the cellar set at Gernika within the Urdaibai biosphere reserve.
wine.making: Made as a selection wine since 2003, by the house's account. After fermentation the wine is kept for several months on its lees in stainless steel, which gives it more body, structure and smoothness than a young txakoli; it is bottled to age for some years rather than to drink at once.
wine.glass: Baked apple, lemon and mandarin over a saline edge, taking on a waxy note with time; broad and almost unctuous for a txakoli, its fresh acidity holding the ripeness.
wine.ageing: Built, by the house's account, to age for several years in bottle: powerful and full of flavour when young, it gains harmony and complexity with time.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius, warmer than a young txakoli; no decanter needed; a white Burgundy glass rather than a tumbler, so its breadth shows.

label.means: The txakoli DO of Bizkaia, recognised in 1994, its vineyards scattered across the province.
Basque for a mountain by the sea, after the slopes that look over the Bay of Biscay.

records.table: Itsasmendi 7 is the Gernika house's fuller white txakoli: Hondarrabi Zuri and Zerratia with a share of Riesling, kept months on its lees in steel. Broad and saline, with baked apple and mandarin, it is built to age and wants a proper white wine glass.
records.story: Itsasmendi takes its name from the Basque for a mountain by the sea, after the slopes that look over the Bay of Biscay. By its own account a group of growers set it up in 1994 to make a txakoli of quality, the year the Bizkaiko Txakolina DO was granted to a province whose small producers had worked for it since the middle of the 1980s. Its first vineyard, by the house's account, was planted at Muskiz in 1989, and it began with vineyards in Muskiz, Bakio and Mendata and a small winery at Muskiz; its first wine is dated 1995. Early in the 2000s the cellar moved to Gernika, within the Urdaibai biosphere reserve: in 2003 by the house's account, in 2001 or 2002 by others. The 2003 vintage brought the first Itsasmendi 7, a selection white made for more body and structure and to age in bottle, which the house calls the first crianza txakoli of its DO. Its blend of Hondarrabi Zuri with Zerratia and Riesling, rested for months on its lees, made a white for the table rather than for the bar. Other wines followed, among them Artizar, aged on its lees in a large French oak vat. For a sommelier Itsasmendi 7 shows what time on the lees and in bottle can do for the grapes of txakoli.

others.name: Itsasmendi
others.note: The house's young white of Hondarrabi Zuri and Hondarrabi Zuri Zerratia, the txakoli of the bar.

others.name: Artizar
others.note: Fermented and aged on its lees in a French oak vat of two thousand litres, the months on the lees varying by vintage.

traps: Itsasmendi 7 is Bizkaiko Txakolina, from the province of Bilbao, not Getariako Txakolina from Gipuzkoa.
Hondarrabi Zuri Zerratia is Petit Courbu under its Basque name, a grape of the French South West, not a clone of Hondarrabi Zuri.
Itsasmendi 7 is made to age for years in bottle, unlike the young txakoli poured from a height in the bars.

cards.front: Itsasmendi 7: which grapes go into it?
cards.back: Mostly Hondarrabi Zuri and Hondarrabi Zuri Zerratia, with a share of Riesling.

cards.front: What does the Basque name of the Gernika house Itsasmendi mean?
cards.back: A mountain by the sea, after the slopes that look over the Bay of Biscay.

questions.q: Itsasmendi 7 is broader and fuller than most txakoli. What in its making gives it that weight?
opts: Several months on its lees in steel
A year in new French oak barrels
Grapes dried on mats before pressing
A long maceration on the skins
questions.exp: The house rests it for several months on its lees in stainless steel, which adds body and smoothness; new oak would add toast and vanilla, which is not this wine's way.

questions.q: By the house's account, in what year was the first Itsasmendi 7 made?
questions.exp: The house and its merchants give 2003 for the first Itsasmendi 7, a selection white made to age; 1994 is the year of the Bizkaiko Txakolina DO and, by its own account, of the house's founding.

report: Searches for this record: 6 of the group's share of 35, one of them spent in vain on the name; no fetch tried; the house's own site was read through search on bodegasitsasmendi.com.

The plan's note: the house's About page says it was created in 1994 by a group of growers and lists the name with 1995, and Vinissimus and an importer give a first wine and a first winery at Muskiz in 1995; founded is empty and the story gives the house's 1994 and the first wine of 1995. The move to Gernika is 2003 on the house's page and 2002 on other pages; the record gives the house's year, hedged. One importer tells of a new winery among the vines in 2019; one source only, left out.

The grapes of 7: Hondarrabi Zuri, Zerratia and Riesling on a merchant's sheet (about two fifths, two fifths and a fifth) and Decanter's note of the 2014 (a fifth Riesling); the house's page searched did not list them. The record says a share of Riesling.

Why 7: no source searched explains the number; a merchant's page tells of a single vineyard wine from 2003 to 2007 and later a selection of seven or nine plots, one source each, left out. The integrator may ask the house.

The house calls 7 the first crianza txakoli of its DO; the claim is hedged as the house's. One merchant says no wood touches it; the record says only steel and lees, on the house's page. Lees time is given as several months, as the house says, where merchants' sheets give seven to eleven.

The glass draws on Decanter (baked apple, lemon, mandarin), Spanish Wine Lover (herbs, a saline edge), the Peñín guide (waxy, saline) and the house (broad, unctuous, acidity balancing ripeness). Not in WINE_PRODUCERS.

wine.name: Gorrondona
wine.grapes: Hondarrabi Zuri, the great majority, with small shares of Hondarrabi Zuri Zerratia and Mune Mahatsa, the Basque Folle Blanche, and a touch of Hondarrabi Beltza.
wine.sites: Several of the estate's plots on the south facing slopes of the Bakio valley, on the coast of Bizkaia north of Bilbao, each picked and fermented apart and blended only after its time on the lees.
wine.making: Picked by hand into small crates and in the cellar within three hours, by the house's sheet. Each plot is fermented apart in stainless steel with its own yeasts, slowly, to keep the aromas, ending with a trace of residual sugar; the wine stays on its lees before the tanks are blended.
wine.glass: Fresh grass, eucalyptus and lemon, with a faint salty edge the house puts down to the sea air; light and dry, with crisp, clean acidity and a short, fresh finish.
wine.ageing: Made to drink young, in the year or two after the harvest, while its grassy freshness is bright; the estate's Doniene is its white for keeping longer.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, as the house's sheet advises; no decanter; a white wine glass, or a Basque tumbler in a bar.

label.means: The txakoli DO of Bizkaia, recognised in 1994, with vineyards on the coast around Bakio and inland.
The farmhouse at Bakio that names the estate and its white for every day.

records.table: Gorrondona is the white of Doniene Gorrondona at Bakio, on the Bizkaia coast: mostly Hondarrabi Zuri, each plot fermented apart with its own yeasts and kept on its lees. Grassy and lemony, with a faint salty edge, it suits anchovies, clams or a first course of fish.
records.story: The Gorrondona farmhouse at Bakio, on the coast of Bizkaia, was built before 1852, and by the estate's own account documents show that txakoli was made there early on. By the Bizkaia provincial government's account, its wine was for the family's own table until the middle of the twentieth century, and it began to be sold in the 1970s. Bakio had long been a centre of Bizkaia's txakoli, and in 1994 the Bizkaiko Txakolina DO was granted for the province, after a decade's work by a small group of its producers. A new team of partners took on the winery in the middle of the 1990s, in 1994 by most accounts, after a study, by the house's account, to revive Bakio as a place of vines; the company dates from 1996 by its own reckoning, and a Bizkaia paper marked its twentieth year in 2016. The partners worked plot by plot with each plot's own yeasts, kept to the grapes of the coast, among them Mune Mahatsa, the old Basque name for Folle Blanche, and recovered old vineyards of Hondarrabi Beltza at Bakio for a young red, Beltza. Gorrondona is the estate's white for every day and Doniene its lees aged white. For a sommelier the house is Bakio's case for txakoli: whites with the salt of the coast, and a rare red from the black grape.

others.name: Doniene
others.note: The estate's lees aged white, kept on its lees and then in bottle before release, from plots on clay, marl and schist.

others.name: Beltza
others.note: A young red of Hondarrabi Beltza alone, from a project to recover old vineyards of Bakio.

others.name: Apardune
others.note: A traditional method sparkling txakoli, Brut Nature with no dosage, aged on its lees in bottle for well over a year before it is disgorged.

traps: Doniene Gorrondona is the estate; Gorrondona is its white for every day and Doniene its lees aged white.
Bakio's wine is Bizkaiko Txakolina; Getariako Txakolina is the DO of Gipuzkoa, the next province to the east.
Beltza is a red of Hondarrabi Beltza alone: txakoli is not only white, though its reds are rare.

cards.front: Doniene Gorrondona: in which coastal town of Bizkaia does the estate lie?
cards.back: Bakio, north of Bilbao, a historic centre of Bizkaia's txakoli.

cards.front: How is the Gorrondona white fermented?
cards.back: Plot by plot in stainless steel, slowly, with each plot's own yeasts, then kept on its lees before the tanks are blended.

questions.q: A guest asks what besides Hondarrabi Zuri goes into Doniene Gorrondona's white, Gorrondona. Which set is right?
opts: Zerratia, Mune Mahatsa and a touch of Beltza
Riesling, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc
Albariño, Treixadura and Loureiro
Viura, Malvasía and Garnacha Blanca
questions.exp: The house's sheets give small shares of Hondarrabi Zuri Zerratia, Mune Mahatsa, the Basque Folle Blanche, and Hondarrabi Beltza; Albariño and its partners are the grapes of Galicia.

questions.q: In what decade did a new team of partners take on the Gorrondona winery at Bakio and set out to revive its vines?
opts: The 1990s
The 1970s
The 1950s
The 2000s
questions.exp: A new team came in the middle of the 1990s, in 1994 by most accounts and as a company in 1996 by the house's; the 1970s are when the farm's wine first began to be sold.

report: Searches for this record: 5 of the group's share of 35, no fetch tried; the house's own site and technical sheets were read through search on donienegorrondona.com.

The plan's note is answered: Gorrondona is the white's name on the house's sheets, mostly Hondarrabi Zuri with small shares of Zerratia, Mune Mahatsa and Beltza in the 2023 and 2024 vintages (91, 5, 3 and 1 per cent); Doniene is the lees aged white on Spanish Wine Lover's page and the house's own sheet for its vineyards.

Founded is 1996, the company's year on the house's page, on Spanish Wine Lover and in Deia's article of 2016 on its twentieth year; one Deia piece gives 1994, the year the house says the present team began, with the DO.

Left out for want of a second source: the Gorrondona brand from the 1970s, the red renamed Beltza with the 2018 vintage and made for more than twenty five years, and the meaning of the name Doniene (one source each).

The house's sheets give its vintage weather, harvest dates, bottle counts and analysis; none is used, as each belongs to one vintage. The soils of the Doniene plots (clay, variegated marl and schist) are from the house's Doniene sheet; no soil is given for Gorrondona itself, so the sites name none.
Living people met and not named: the partners who bought the winery in 1996. Not in WINE_PRODUCERS.

wine.name: Astobiza
wine.grapes: Hondarrabi Zuri, alone by the house's shop sheet, though other pages of the house give about a tenth of Hondarrabi Zuri Zerratia.
wine.sites: The estate's one vineyard around the winery at Okondo, planted from 1996 at about 250 metres on the south facing slope of Mount Ganekogorta, sheltered by the Sierra Salvada; its seven small plots are picked and made apart.
wine.making: Picked by hand into small crates with a double selection, then fermented at a controlled temperature in stainless steel under inert gas. The wine rests on its fine lees for six to eight months, and for six to eight months more in bottle before release, by the house's sheet.
wine.glass: Pale straw with green glints; pear, apple, grapefruit and white peach, fresh and balanced, ending long with a light bitter, stony touch.
wine.ageing: Ready at release, after its months on the lees and in bottle, and fresh for a few years after; Malkoa, aged in concrete eggs, is the estate's white for laying down.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, as the house advises; no decanter; a white wine glass, with sushi, raw fish or cold shellfish.

label.means: The txakoli DO of Álava, in the Ayala valley inland of Bilbao, recognised by an order of 2 April 2001.
The estate at Okondo whose name the wine carries; Señorío de Astobiza is the estate's full name.

records.table: Astobiza is the white of an estate at Okondo, in Álava's inland txakoli country of the Ayala valley: Hondarrabi Zuri from one vineyard planted from 1996, kept months on its fine lees and then in bottle. Pear, grapefruit and white peach end on a light bitter touch.
records.story: The Ayala valley in the north of Álava lies on the Atlantic side of the mountains, its rivers running north to Bilbao, and its txakoli was the last of the three to win a DO. Arabako Txakolina was recognised by an order of the Basque government of 2 April 2001, for Amurrio, Artziniega, Ayala, Llodio and Okondo. Señorío de Astobiza began earlier, as a family project of 1996, when the first vines were planted on the estate near Okondo, at about 250 metres on the southern slope of Mount Ganekogorta, sheltered, as the house tells it, by the Sierra Salvada and some twenty kilometres from the sea. In 2007 by the house's account, in 2008 by others, the estate built its own winery among those vines. It works, in its own words, with native grapes only, Hondarrabi Zuri above all, with Hondarrabi Beltza and Izkiriota, the Basque name for Gros Manseng, and it divides its one vineyard into seven small plots, each picked and made apart. Astobiza, the white, rests months on its fine lees and then in bottle before it is sold; Malkoa, aged in concrete eggs, is the white for keeping, and a late harvest wine stands beside them. For a sommelier Astobiza is the way into Arabako Txakolina: the inland txakoli of one valley rather than the coast, from a single estate and its own vines.

others.name: Malkoa
others.note: The estate's white for laying down, aged about twenty months in concrete eggs, by the house's sheet.

others.name: Astobiza Vendimia Tardía
others.note: The estate's late harvest wine, of Izkiriota, the Basque name for Gros Manseng, made only in some years.

traps: Arabako Txakolina is the txakoli of the Ayala valley in northern Álava; the south of Álava is Rioja Alavesa, in the Rioja DOCa.
Izkiriota is the Basque name for Gros Manseng, a grape of the French South West, not a local crossing.
Arabako Txakolina, recognised in 2001, is the last of the three txakoli DOs, not the first, which is Getaria's of 1989.

cards.front: Señorío de Astobiza: where are its vines, and from when were they planted?
cards.back: Around the winery at Okondo in the Ayala valley of Álava, on the south slope of Mount Ganekogorta, from 1996.

cards.front: Where does the Astobiza white rest before it is sold?
cards.back: On its fine lees in stainless steel for some months, then in bottle for some months more.

questions.q: A guest pours a bottle of Astobiza from Okondo. Which DO does its label carry?
opts: Arabako Txakolina
Getariako Txakolina
Bizkaiko Txakolina
Rioja
questions.exp: Okondo lies in the Ayala valley of northern Álava, the zone of Arabako Txakolina; Rioja covers the south of Álava beyond the Sierra de Cantabria, and Bizkaiko the province of Bilbao.

questions.q: Señorío de Astobiza planted its first vines in 1996. In what year, by its own account, did it build its winery?
questions.exp: The house dates its winery to 2007, among the vines planted from 1996, though some merchants give 2008; 2001 is the year the Arabako Txakolina DO was recognised, and 1994 that of Bizkaia's.

report: Searches for this record: 4 of the group's share of 35, no fetch tried; the house's own site was read through search on astobiza.es, and the Arabako Txakolina DO through the Basque government's pages on euskadi.eus.

The plan's note: the house dates the family project and the first planting to 1996 and its winery to 2007 (its own page, Spanish Wine Lover and Turismo Vasco), while Field Blend Selections says the winery was built in 2008 for the first vintage; founded is empty, as the plan allowed, and the story gives 1996 and the house's 2007.

The grapes: the house's shop sheet gives Hondarrabi Zuri alone; its magnum page and an older wine page give nine tenths Hondarrabi Zuri with a tenth of Zerratia; Izkiriota is told on the house's pages and Alliance Wine's for the estate, not for this wine, so the record keeps it out of the bottle.
Label: the shop sells the wine as Astobiza Blanco and merchants as Señorío de Astobiza; the record prints Astobiza and the DO only.

Left out for want of a second source: that the wine was made in other cellars of the valley before 2007 (Spanish Wine Lover only), the grape of the late harvest wine, the estate's membership of Grandes Pagos de España (an association, so volatile), and any meaning of the name Astobiza.
Living people met and not named: the founder of the family project of 1996. Not in WINE_PRODUCERS.

For the group: nothing found in tension with the Codex's region record for txakoli, which lists Talai Berri where this group has Txomin Etxaniz; the group's searches came to 27 of its share of 35, one fetch tried and refused.
